evidence: Every graded leg is traced to a public statement with a single reasonable reading, and each capability is reachable. Seed: /assets/seed_data.json holds the 5 accounts, M-11/M-12/M-13, the timers, the walled list (dev on M-12, matching 'Dev Anand is walled from M-12 today'), the holds, the versions (K-2 'Landlords notice recieved.', K-13 '2,400') and read_up_to. Every seeded fixture the criteria name exists, and the retention arithmetic matches the brief's rules: K-1 (1 May, 7d) gone; K-10 at exactly 7d gone and K-11 one second younger kept ('a message sent exactly seven days ago on a seven-day matter is already gone'); K-17 (3 May, held) removed on release; K-13/K-18 removed when the timer is shortened to 7d ('editing a message doesn't make it any younger'); timer options [null,1,7,30] match 'off, 1 day, 7 days or 30 days'. Runtime: integration.md's Node 22, Express and better-sqlite3 via NODE_PATH, 0.0.0.0:3000, DB_PATH, env -i with HOME not /app and no symlinks all match test.sh, which is identical to the template (setsid env -i ... setpriv uid 65534 node /app/server.js; the symlink scan is less strict than the brief's 'no symbolic links'). The verifier tests/Dockerfile installs the same express@5.1.0/better-sqlite3@12.4.1, and /assets is a declared artifact. Live updates (polling/SSE), idempotent sends, the clipboard copy-link and browser self-testing (Playwright/Chromium via npm) are all reachable with public network (network_mode=public in both phases). Wording: search 'looks for exactly the characters typed' supports the substring and literal %,_,* legs; 'Only a partner' covers timers and holds; walls 'nothing they do after that reaches it' plus 'nobody can reply from one matter to a message in another' covers the wall replays, and the JUDGE-W3 leg accepts either refusal or same-matter filing. 'A plain not available' matches the plain not-available legs. The transcript bullets (heading, oldest-first threads, author, sent time, edited, hold mark, held-and-edited versions, placeholder) match search_and_transcript and edits leg 4. Unread semantics, the new-messages line, mark-unread 'moves the line there' and 'deleted messages don't count' match unread_and_new_messages_line. The polish rows map to explicit sentences (Enter/Shift+Enter, Escape, confirm-before-delete, highlight 'until you open something else', 390 px, refusal reason 'stays until you change it'). Achievability on these bytes: the raw-evidence hashes verify against the frozen source, and golden-run.log shows all 16 functional criteria, the constraints gate, persistence before and after a real process restart, and the 6 polish criteria PASS under uid 65534/env -i. That is a scripted run, not a configured judge run. The prior-bytes hosted GPT-5.6 failures (mention regex bug, time-based read marker, missing transcript versions) are implementation bugs against explicit text, not ambiguity. Non-blocking notes: (1) the brief never says 'sign out', but signin_and_client_scope and polish refusal_in_place sign out. Switching people from the pages ('sign in as different people') implies it, and SKILL.md lists the identity surface as a known false positive. (2) Stale edit: 'because the message changed since they opened it' could, read very literally, let an app that rebases an open edit box's version on a live update accept the stale save. The purpose clause 'refuse the edit and keep what they typed so they can look again' makes the refuse reading the only sensible one. (3) The deleted-parent placeholder may be drawn as a parent node above the reply or as a replacement quote; both satisfy 'above them we just want to see that the original message was deleted', and the criterion wording ('in place of a quote') should not be read as excluding the former.
